title: Can one hundred be one square minus another square?
description: The rule for one square minus another is read backwards, so one hundred is first split into two even numbers multiplied. The board finds the two squares from their sum and their take away, and puts the answer back to check. The video breaks the idea that no whole numbers can work.
teaching_notes: One idea: split the number into two even numbers multiplied, set them equal to eigh plus b and eigh minus b, and find eigh and b. Watch for students who pick two numbers that multiply to one hundred but do not both come out even.

source: Figure it Out (squares and patterns, question 2)
video_script.why: The child can turn a sum times a take away into one square minus another, but has not yet run the rule backwards from a number.
video_script.substitution: Split the number into two even numbers multiplied, and match them to eigh plus b and eigh minus b, as the example in the book used that rule.
video_script.anchor: the number one hundred, split into two numbers multiplied
video_script.payoff_line: One hundred is twenty six squared minus twenty four squared.

final_answer.spoken: twenty six squared minus twenty four squared

maths_rules: 100 = 50 × 2; both numbers even, so a and b are whole
a + b = 50 and a − b = 2; adding gives 2a = 52, so a = 26
video_script.design: One idea: run the rule backwards by splitting the number into two even numbers multiplied. The rule card stays through the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Your book gave a rule. Eigh squared minus b squared is eigh plus b times eigh minus b.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write one hundred as one square minus another square.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, write one hundred as two numbers multiplied, to match the rule. We take fifty times two.
<bookmark mark='even'/>Both numbers are even, so that eigh and b will come out whole.

beats.on_screen: a + b = 50 and a − b = 2; adding: 2a = 52, so a = 26

marks.match: a + b = 50 and a − b = 2 are written

beats.colours: the sum and the take away in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='match'/>Step two, let eigh plus b be fifty, and eigh minus b be two.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Adding the two lines, the b terms cancel, and two eigh is fifty two.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Half of fifty two gives eigh equal to twenty six.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Step three, b is fifty minus twenty six. That is twenty four.
<bookmark mark='squares'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question. Twenty six squared is six hundred seventy six, and twenty four squared is five hundred seventy six.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Six hundred seventy six minus five hundred seventy six is one hundred.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>One hundred is twenty six squared minus twenty four squared.
<bookmark mark='other'/>Taking ten times ten gives another way, ten squared minus zero squared.
